lessons.title: Evictable large-value cache
lessons.objective: Cache and retrieve one bounded blob while keeping provider availability, authority, retention, integrity, and eviction outcomes explicit.
lessons.prose: Cache nodes cross an ordinary bounded host-service boundary. Put returns an opaque provider- and run-scoped handle; get verifies the content digest before yielding bytes; remove invalidates one handle. The installed provider is best effort and evictable, never durable, and a handle never substitutes for a grant.
lessons.source:
panel 0

node blob : storage/blob/literal {
    value = bytes("626f756e64656420636163686520666978747572650a")
    maximum_bytes = 64
}

node put : storage/cache/put {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-put")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-put")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 10
    retention_ticks = 100
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    persistence = "evictable"
    eviction = "fifo"
    sensitivity = "restricted"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

node get : storage/cache/get {
    resource = secret("conduit.resource/storage-cache-example-get")
    grant = secret("conduit.grant/storage-cache-get")
    descriptor = ref("conduit.descriptor/storage-cache-example")
    run_epoch = 1
    now_tick = 11
    maximum_blob_bytes = 64
    integrity = "sha256-before-yield"
    cancellation = "discard"
}

cord blob.blob -> put.blob { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 64 max_queued_bytes = 64 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
cord put.handle -> get.handle { capacity = 1 max_value_bytes = 66 max_queued_bytes = 66 low_watermark = 0 high_watermark = 1 pressure = block }
hints: The handle is an opaque reference scoped to this provider and run; get still needs its own active grant.
Best effort describes the provider class, while a fresh host observation describes current selectability. Neither promises future uptime.
A hit validates SHA-256 identity before bytes cross the output cord; miss, eviction, expiration, provider loss, and cancellation remain distinct outcomes.
lessons.solution: Wire an explicitly bounded blob into put, pass only its opaque handle to get or remove, pin a fresh provider report and separate operation grants in the exact plan, and request evictable retention only.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table names provider observation freshness, best-effort class, resource and grant, blob digest and byte count, opaque handle scope, queue pressure, retention, hit or miss, cancellation, error, and terminal cause.
accessibility.keyboard: Native controls plus Space to play and ArrowRight to step while the ordered cache story has focus.
accessibility.color_independent: Every state is duplicated by provider, handle, digest, bound, hit, miss, evicted, expired, cancelled, error, and terminal text.

lessons.objective: Probe one content-addressed WAVE fixture through an exact bounded provider, then compose encode, mux, demux, and decode without format guessing or hidden buffering.

Malformed or truncated bytes, timestamp reorder, overflow, cancellation during flush, and an unavailable provider terminate explicitly without partial output.

Checking it offline proves that the authored document is well formed; it does not prove that this machine has a provider or authority. Resolve creates a separate exact plan. Starting that plan creates a live epoch. Execution appends bounded evidence. Editing source or moving a box never rewrites an already admitted plan, live epoch, or evidence record.
lessons.expected_display: PROGRAM, PLAN, LIVE STATE, AND EVIDENCE STAY DISTINCT.

validation.value: PROGRAM, PLAN, LIVE STATE, AND EVIDENCE STAY DISTINCT.

hints: Move a node: only the presentation identity changes.

Check can succeed offline even when a referenced optional provider or artifact is unavailable.
lessons.solution: Review source, lock, and artifact-reference changes as program changes; resolve them into a distinct exact plan; admit a new epoch through the ordinary transition; and read bounded evidence without treating it as source.

accessibility.non_audio: An ordered text table labels program source, exact plan, live epoch, and evidence as four separate identities and states which operation can change each one.
accessibility.keyboard: Tab moves through program, plan, live epoch, and evidence; ArrowRight steps through existing evidence only.
accessibility.color_independent: Each layer has a written name, identity, and change rule; color is never the only distinction.

lessons.title: Imports name meaning; plans provide machines
lessons.objective: Compare a friendly source alias with its exact canonical contract identity, then distinguish successful offline import checking from provider availability.
lessons.prose: The alias split is source-local; conduit.dev/std/tee is the package-owned semantic identity and its descriptor hash pins the exact contract: imports name the part; the plan determines whether a particular machine can provide it. Import resolution reads only the supplied contract-package bytes and lock, never a URL, package registry, installer, grant, or provider selector.
lessons.source:
panel 0

import conduit.dev/std/{tee as split}

# The import can check offline while this selected host has no provider.
node branch : split
hints: Select split to reveal conduit.dev/std/tee and its pinned descriptor hash.
Switch to the missing-export scenario to see deterministic CND-IPK-004 source-span evidence.
Notice that successful import checking adds no installed provider, host grant, or authority.
lessons.solution: Supply the immutable package artifact and exact lock to the checker, retain the alias only for presentation, and let later exact planning decide whether current host facts permit a provider binding.

accessibility.keyboard: Tab moves through source alias, resolved identity, availability, and error scenarios.
accessibility.color_independent: Every state is written as text with an exact identity or diagnostic code.
